prompt: What does a vulnerability scanner like Trivy actually do with an image?

choices.text: Runs the program and tries known attacks against it
choices.why: It never runs or attacks anything.

choices.text: Compares it with the newest image under the same tag
choices.why: It compares with a database of advisories, not with other images.

choices.text: Lists its contents and looks each up in advisories
choices.why: Right: an inventory, then a lookup.

choices.text: Checks its signature
choices.why: Signatures are a different tool, Cosign.

prompt: The same image, unchanged, is scanned a month later and shows more findings. Why?

choices.text: The image decays as it is pulled
choices.why: An image's bytes never change; its digest proves it.

choices.text: Trivy finds more with each run on the same image
choices.why: Its results depend on the database, not on repetition.

choices.text: Docker updated packages inside it
choices.why: Nothing updates an image's contents.

choices.text: The advisory database grew
choices.why: Right: new advisories name packages the image always had.

prompt: How many known vulnerabilities did Trivy report in `debian:trixie-slim`? Add up the severities.
`shelf` never imports `golang.org/x/text`, yet Trivy found it in the `shelf` binary. How?
hint: What does every Go binary carry?

choices.text: The binary embeds the modules it was built from
choices.why: Right, and `x/text` came in with `pgx`.

choices.text: It guessed from the binary's size
choices.why: Trivy reads exact versions; it does not guess.

choices.text: It read `go.mod` from the image
choices.why: The final image has no `go.mod`; only the binaries.

choices.text: Distroless lists Go modules in its package records
choices.why: Those records are Debian's packages, not Go modules.

prompt: Match each target in the `shelf` report to what Trivy read for it.

pairs.right: The modules built into the server
The modules built into the health check

prompt: `--ignore-unfixed` reduced Debian's 163 findings to none. What does that tell Ana?
hint: What would a rebuild today change?

choices.text: The image is safe
choices.why: The vulnerabilities are still there; they just have no fix yet.

choices.text: A rebuild today would remove none of them
choices.why: Right: they go when Debian ships fixes.

choices.text: Trivy's database is too old to know of the fixes
choices.why: It is a day old; the fixes do not exist yet.

choices.text: Debian will never fix them
choices.why: `affected` means not fixed yet, not never.

prompt: To make Trivy fail a pipeline step when it finds something, add `--___ 1`.
hint: The status the command ends with.

prompt: Put Ana's fix for the `x/text` finding in order.
hint: Change the dependency, then prove it.

prompt: After the update, `shelf` still had one finding: `tzdata` in the base, fixed in Debian. What gets rid of it?

choices.text: `go get` a newer `tzdata`
choices.why: `tzdata` is a Debian package in the base, not a Go module.

choices.text: `--ignore-unfixed`
choices.why: It is fixed upstream; the flag would not hide it, and hiding is not fixing.

choices.text: A rebuilt distroless, then a rebuild of `shelf`
choices.why: Right; with the base pinned, a pull request brings the new digest.

choices.text: Deleting `/usr/share/zoneinfo` in a later layer
choices.why: Lesson 14: a later layer hides files and keeps them.

prompt: Why is `--severity HIGH,CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed` the usual gate, rather than failing on every finding?

choices.text: Low findings are always false positives
choices.why: They are real advisories, just less severe.

choices.text: Trivy cannot report low findings in CI
choices.why: It reports every severity unless told not to.

choices.text: Unfixed findings are never exploitable
choices.why: They can be; there is just nothing to upgrade to yet.

choices.text: It blocks what has a fix, not what has none
choices.why: Right: a gate nobody can pass gets switched off.

prompt: The index for `shelf:1.6.0` listed a manifest with platform `unknown/unknown`. What is it?

choices.text: The attestations about the `linux/amd64` image
choices.why: Right: SBOM and provenance, pointing at the image by digest.

choices.text: A broken build for an unrecognised CPU
choices.why: Nothing failed; it is not an image at all.

choices.text: An image for any platform
choices.why: No platform runs it.

choices.text: A copy kept for rollback
choices.why: Rollback uses older digests, not this.

prompt: An advisory appears next month for a package. How does an SBOM kept for each release help?
hint: Which question does it answer without pulling anything?

choices.text: It patches the package automatically
choices.why: An SBOM is a list; it changes nothing.

choices.text: It answers which images contain it
choices.why: Right, without pulling and scanning every image again.

choices.text: It blocks the vulnerable image from running
choices.why: Blocking is a policy's job, not a list's.

choices.text: It proves the package was never used
choices.why: It lists what is present, not what is used.

prompt: What did the provenance of `shelf:1.6.0` record? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The `golang:1.25` image used, by digest
choices.why: Yes, though the Dockerfile wrote only a tag.

choices.text: The distroless base, by digest
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: The Git commit that was built
Ana's registry password
choices.why: No: there was no password, and provenance does not record one.

prompt: Attestations say what an image is. What does a Cosign signature add?

choices.text: A list of the image's packages
choices.why: That is the SBOM.

choices.text: A scan result
choices.why: Scanning is Trivy's part.

choices.text: Who vouches for the digest
choices.why: Right: verify it is the identity you expect before running.

choices.text: Proof the image has no vulnerabilities
choices.why: A signature says nothing about vulnerabilities.

prompt: Ana writes the team's rule for images. Which one follows this lesson?
hint: Gate what can be fixed, keep the records, check who built it.

choices.text: Fail on any finding at all, of any severity
choices.why: Debian's 161 unfixable ones would block every build.

choices.text: Scan once at release, and never again
choices.why: The database grows; an old scan says nothing about today.

choices.text: Trust any image from a well-known registry
choices.why: Where it is stored says nothing about what is in it.

choices.text: Gate on fixable high findings, keep SBOMs, verify signatures
choices.why: Right: each part answers one of the lesson's questions.
